lore_anchors.definition: A talisman that completely immobilizes a target’s body while preserving full consciousness. Han Li double-tags ‘Qu Hun’ before leaving, showing his paranoid discipline.
Han Li’s versatile defensive magical tool; its clean bisection by an unseen monster signals the sudden escalation of threat level in this chapter.

A forbidden art that temporarily raises a cultivator’s cultivation level at the cost of near-immediate meridians-shattering death. Used by the Devil Dao to manufacture believable fake Core Formation combatants.
The condensed spiritual essence of a cultivator. The Yuling elder survived his original body’s destruction by fleeing in his Primordial Spirit, a standard high-level survival mechanism in xianxia.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li still go to the cave after being suspicious?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was suspicious, but the jade slip was the only physical proof that could verify ‘Qu Hun’s’ story. He calculated the risk and went anyway, trusting his defensive tools to buy him reaction time. The trap was designed to nullify exactly that assumption.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is ‘Qu Hun’ working with the monster, or is this a third party?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is almost certainly ‘Qu Hun’s’ trap. The cave location and the jade slip story came from him, and the pile of gnawed bones suggests he has been feeding the monster. The ambush is a pre-arranged failsafe in case Han Li became hostile or suspicious.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the White Phosphorus Shield being sliced in half?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The White Phosphorus Shield has been Han Li’s go-to defensive tool since the Blood Forbidden Land arc, surviving attacks from Foundation Establishment enemies and talisman treasures. Its clean bisection without any transmitted force signals that the monster’s attack is qualitatively different—something Han Li has not faced before.
